decks.title: Highlights of India
decks.kicker: Swipe through the best of Bharat

slides.line: Shah Jahan's white-marble tribute to Mumtaz Mahal — see it blush pink at sunrise.
A gilded sanctum on a sacred pool, where the free langar kitchen feeds everyone who comes.
Evening Ganga aarti on the ghats of one of the world's oldest living cities.
A lake above 4,200 m that shifts from turquoise to deep blue as the light changes.
Drift through palm-fringed canals and stay the night on a kettuvallam houseboat.
A living fort of golden sandstone rising out of the Thar Desert.
Boulder hills strewn with the ruins of the Vijayanagara capital — a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
A bridge grown, not built: Khasi villagers train rubber-fig roots across the stream.
Home to about two-thirds of the world's greater one-horned rhinos.
Buddhist rock-cut caves with paintings spanning the 2nd century BCE to about 480 CE.
Ten days of Naga dance, song and food at Kisama, every 1–10 December.
Ride the gondola into the snow — Kashmir's meadow of flowers turns ski resort in winter.
Tigers prowl beneath the walls of the ancient Ranthambore Fort.
A 13th-century temple carved as the Sun god's colossal stone chariot, wheels and all.
White sand and glass-clear water at Radhanagar Beach in the Andaman Sea.
A UNESCO-listed alpine valley that bursts into bloom in the monsoon.
Towering gopurams covered in thousands of brightly painted figures.
A high cold desert of cliff-top monasteries and moonscape roads.

decks.title: Must-do Adventure
decks.kicker: Thrills from the Himalaya to the Andaman Sea

slides.line: Ride the Ganga's white-water rapids down to Rishikesh.
slides.title: White-water rafting, Rishikesh

slides.line: Paraglide off Billing over the Kangra valley — a Paragliding World Cup venue.
slides.title: Paragliding at Bir Billing

slides.line: Walk the frozen Zanskar River in the depths of the Ladakh winter.
Learn to dive among the coral reefs of the Andaman Sea.
slides.title: Scuba diving, Andamans

slides.line: A classic winter summit trek through snow-laden pine forest.
Skiing in winter, paragliding and zorbing in summer — just above Manali.
Trek to a pass face-to-face with Kangchenjunga, the world's third-highest peak.
Walk from Sankri into a hanging valley of meadows ringed by Garhwal snow peaks.
White water on the Kundalika, fed by morning releases from a dam upstream.
Two days from Aru to an almond-shaped alpine lake at 3,795 m.
Ride one of the world's highest cable cars to powder runs near 4,000 m.
slides.title: Skiing off the Gulmarg Gondola

slides.line: Paddle the Zanskar's canyon from Chiling to its meeting with the Indus at Nimmu.
slides.title: Rafting the Zanskar gorge

slides.line: An 8–10 hour climb, rated one of South India's toughest and most rewarding treks.
slides.title: Summit Kumara Parvatha

slides.line: Walk deep into India's second-longest cave system, past stalactites and underground chambers.
slides.title: Go underground at Belum

slides.line: Climb before dawn to the top of the Barail Range for a sunrise over Kohima's hills.
slides.title: Sunrise on Mount Japfü

slides.line: Ride up to 5,359 m on one of the world's highest motorable roads, gateway to Nubra.
slides.title: Ride over Khardung La

slides.line: Shoot the Kali's rapids through the forests of Dandeli.
slides.title: White water on the Kali

slides.line: Cross a 4,220 m pass above the Parvati Valley — and slide down the snow on the other side.
slides.title: Slide down from Sar Pass

slides.line: Launch off the Western Ghats near Lonavala, Maharashtra's paragliding hub.
slides.title: Fly at Kamshet

slides.line: Hike up the Parvati valley from Barshaini and soak in a hot spring at the top.
Monsoon white-water through the forests of south Coorg.

decks.title: Must-do Festivals
decks.kicker: Time your trip to India's greatest celebrations

slides.line: Nagaland's tribes gather at Kisama for the "festival of festivals".
Camel trading, folk music and fairground on the desert's edge around Kartik Purnima.
Lathmar Holi: in Radha's village, women playfully drive men off with sticks.
slides.title: Lathmar Holi, Barsana

slides.line: Kolkata turns into an open-air gallery of art-filled pandals — UNESCO-listed heritage.
slides.title: Durga Puja, Kolkata

slides.line: Caparisoned elephants, a duel of bright parasols and thundering percussion.
Giant chariots of Lord Jagannath hauled by crowds down Puri's Grand Road.
slides.title: Rath Yatra, Puri

slides.line: Snake boats with around a hundred rowers each race on Punnamada Lake.
A tent city on the white salt desert of Kutch — magical under a full moon.
The Apatani people of Ziro pray for a good harvest over three days each July.
slides.title: Dree in the Ziro valley

slides.line: Sikkim's Bhutia harvest new year, ushered in with masked cham dances.
slides.title: Losoong, Sikkim

slides.line: Manipur's five-day spring festival — sports by day, Thabal Chongba dances by moonlight.
slides.title: Spring in Imphal for Yaoshang

slides.line: Watch bull-tamers try to cling to charging bulls in Alanganallur's famous arena, the highlight of Pongal.
slides.title: Jallikattu at Alanganallur

slides.line: A huge ghee beacon is lit on the summit of Arunachala as the town below glows with lamps.
slides.title: The beacon on Arunachala

slides.line: Walk a stretch with the Varkari pilgrims, singing abhangs on the road to Vithoba.
slides.title: Walk the Wari

slides.line: Join Gujarat on its rooftops at Makar Sankranti, when kites fill the sky.
slides.title: Fly kites at Uttarayan

slides.line: Long snake boats glide down the Pamba to the songs of their oarsmen at Onam.
slides.title: Snake boats at Aranmula

slides.line: A whole town turns into a stage for the story of Krishna and Kansa.
slides.title: Theatre the size of a town

decks.title: Must-do Wildlife
decks.kicker: Tigers, rhinos, lions and a sky full of birds

slides.line: Jeep safaris in search of tigers among ruined chhatris and lakes.
slides.title: Tigers at Ranthambore

slides.line: Elephant-grass plains holding most of the world's one-horned rhinos.
slides.title: Rhinos at Kaziranga

slides.line: The last wild home of the Asiatic lion.
slides.title: Asiatic lions of Gir

slides.line: Boat safaris through the mangrove delta of the Bengal tiger.
India's oldest national park, founded in 1936 — tigers, elephants and the Ramganga.
Sal forest and meadows where the hard-ground barasingha was saved from extinction.
Cycle through Bharatpur's wetland, winter home to thousands of migratory birds.
slides.title: Birding at Bharatpur

slides.line: Blackbuck herds on open grassland by the Gulf of Khambhat.
Every autumn, migrating Amur falcons roost in huge flocks around Pangti — the "Falcon Capital of the World".
Climb the Zabarwan slopes above Srinagar looking for the hangul, the rare Kashmir stag.
Tall Dooars grassland where one-horned rhinos graze below the Himalayan foothills.
The Mahanadi slices a 22 km gorge through the forested Eastern Ghats.
Misty Kalimpong forests known for the elusive red panda.

slides.key: GJ|Marine National Park, Gulf of Kutch
slides.line: At low tide, walk out over the Narara reef to find corals and sea creatures in the pools.
Watch the Ganga aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat, then a dawn boat ride.
slides.title: Ganga aarti, Varanasi

slides.line: Join the langar — volunteers serve free meals round the clock.
Sit beneath the Bodhi Tree where the Buddha attained enlightenment.
Trek to one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, high in the Garhwal Himalaya.
One of the Char Dham — home of the Rath Yatra and its famous temple kitchen.
India's largest monastery, at about 3,000 m above the Tawang valley.
Qawwali at the shrine of the Sufi saint Moinuddin Chishti.
Jain temples of white marble carved so finely the ceilings look like lace.
The gurdwara at the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh, one of Sikhism's five takhts.

decks.title: Must-do Heritage
decks.kicker: Forts, stepwells and temples carved from rock

slides.line: The Kailasa temple — carved top-down out of a single basalt cliff.
Mirror-work halls in a hilltop fort above Maota Lake.
Temples covered in some of India's finest medieval sculpture.
An 11th-century stepwell with hundreds of sculptures — pictured on the ₹100 note.
Rajaraja Chola's great granite temple, completed in 1010 CE.
A 72.5 m tower of fluted sandstone, begun around 1199.
Wander the bazaars, temples and royal enclosures of the Vijayanagara empire.
Some 3,500 steps zig-zag 30 m down this 8th–9th-century stepwell at Abhaneri.
An 11th-century Chaulukya temple to Surya, carved from top to bottom.
Walk the sea walls of a 1535 Portuguese fortress ringed by a double moat.
slides.title: Diu's sea fort

slides.line: An Afghan emperor's red-sandstone mausoleum rising from its lake at Sasaram.
Giant gods carved into jungle cliffs above the Gomati river.
slides.title: Boat to the cliff gods of Chabimura

slides.line: Shikara rides past houseboats and floating gardens in Srinagar.
Boats seem to float in mid-air on the glass-clear Umngot.
Sand dunes and double-humped camels beneath the Karakoram.
Tea gardens rolling over the hills of the Western Ghats.
One of the highest lakes in the world, held sacred by Buddhists and Sikhs.
India's tallest plunge waterfall, near Cherrapunji.
Camel rides and a Thar Desert sunset outside Jaisalmer.
A basalt plateau that turns into carpets of wildflowers after the monsoon — part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
A high lake at 4,522 m on the Changthang plateau, where black-necked cranes come to breed.
Hike the Shirui hills while the lily that grows wild nowhere else is in bloom.
slides.title: Find the Shirui lily

slides.line: A 91 m single plunge of white water in the forests of Bastar's Kanger Valley.
Look up at the Milky Way from India's first dark-sky reserve, beside the Indian Astronomical Observatory.
slides.title: Stargaze at Hanle

slides.line: Camp by the crescent Moon Lake at 4,250 m in Lahaul.
slides.title: Camp by Chandra Taal

slides.line: Boat between glowing white marble cliffs on the Narmada — best on a full-moon night.
slides.title: Moonlight at the Marble Rocks

slides.line: Stuffed, deep-fried parathas in a Chandni Chowk lane — then chaat and jalebi.
slides.title: Street food in Chandni Chowk

slides.line: Dum-cooked biryani in the city of the Nizams.
Vada pav, pav bhaji and bhel puri by the sea.
Melt-in-the-mouth galouti kebabs and slow-cooked Awadhi dum.
Amritsari kulcha and tall glasses of lassi.
A ceremonial multi-course feast, from rogan josh to gushtaba.
Fiery, spice-rich cooking from the mansion towns around Karaikudi.
Pull over on the highway north of Delhi for paranthas dripping with white butter.
Galouti kebabs so soft they melt — a Lucknow institution since 1905.
slides.title: Galouti kebabs at Tunday's

slides.line: Odisha's 'burnt cheese' — fresh chhena baked into a sweet, smoky cake.
slides.title: Chhena poda, Odisha

slides.line: Sip first-flush Darjeeling where it grows — India's first GI-tagged product, on an estate dating to 1854.
slides.title: Tea on the slopes of Darjeeling

slides.line: Queue in Ramzan for slow-cooked haleem, India's first GI-tagged meat dish.
slides.title: Haleem nights in Hyderabad

slides.line: Ahmedabad's old square turns into a food street after 9:30 pm.
slides.title: Midnight snacks at Manek Chowk

slides.line: Cool off with Madurai's milk, almond gum and ice-cream drink.
slides.title: A glass of jigarthanda

slides.line: End a Varanasi evening with the city's GI-tagged betel-leaf paan.
slides.title: Banarasi paan by the ghats

slides.line: Malabar's own biryani — small, fragrant kaima rice instead of basmati.
Eromba, singju and purple-black chak-hao kheer, all built on rice and fermented ngari.
Bardhaman's twin GI-tagged sweets: golden grains of mihidana and rice-like sitabhog.

decks.title: Must-do Arts & Crafts
decks.kicker: Meet the makers behind India's crafts

slides.line: See cloth hand-printed with carved wooden blocks around Jaipur.
A heritage crafts village where homes double as pattachitra studios.
Mithila painting in bold lines and bright natural colours.
Temple-town silk saris with heavy zari borders.
Brocade saris woven on handlooms in Varanasi.
Crafts and food from every state in one open-air market.
Tribal paintings of circles, triangles and lines that tell village stories.
Two weeks every February of handlooms, crafts, folk music and food from India and abroad.
Watch Bastar artisans cast bell-metal figures by the lost-wax method.
slides.title: Dhokra casting, Bastar

slides.line: Black pots of crushed stone and clay, shaped by hand without a wheel in a Tangkhul Naga village.
slides.title: Watch Longpi pots take shape

slides.line: Wander the lanes where Kolkata's potters shape the clay idols for Durga Puja.
slides.title: Idol-makers of Kumartuli

slides.line: See temple icons cast in bronze by the lost-wax method, as in Chola times.
slides.title: Bronze casters of Swamimalai

slides.line: Watch castor-oil paste drawn out into fine patterns on cloth with a metal stylus.
slides.title: Rogan painting in Kutch

slides.line: Look for embroidery so fine it looks the same on both sides, a Chamba wedding gift.
slides.title: The Chamba rumal
